explanation: A poetic book in the Old Testament that expresses love between a man and a woman, often interpreted allegorically as the love between God and his people.
The woman who is loved by the man in the Song of Songs, often symbolizing God's people or the believing soul.
The man who loves the woman in the Song of Songs, can represent God or Christ who loves his people.
A deep devotion and feeling of closeness between two persons, used in the Song of Songs to describe the relationship between God and humanity.
An image used in the Song of Songs to represent the place where love blooms and grows, can also symbolize Israel or the church.
A country in the Middle East mentioned in the Song of Songs, representing beauty and fertility in nature and in love.
The king of Israel and assumed author of the Song of Songs, associated with wisdom and wealth.
An affectionate nickname used by the groom for his beloved in the Song of Songs, emphasizing the close relationship between the two.
